assumptions: How the closing month's share is counted is in none of the five price lists read: SLATE counts the days of the month the account was open, from the 1st or the day it opened in that month, through the closing day, over the month's days, and rounds half up to the cent, in the bank's own money first. Recorded in closingFeesDue's comment as SLATE's reading.
The month is the save's calendar month (America/New_York for a home account), as every month's end and fee in SLATE is.
A waiver or lower fee is read as the month stands at the close (Postbank's and ING's money paid in so far, Commerzbank's balance), as feeFor reads it on any day.

§ 675h(3) is applied to every close that settles fees: Close It, a bank's own close (closedByBank, closeForOverdraft, homeCloses), a switch; Directive (EU) 2015/2366 art. 55(4), which it carries, isn't limited to ordinary termination. A cancellation in the cooling-off period is charged the same share as § 357b(2)'s Wertersatz on the contract's price, as Commerzbank's own withdrawal notice describes it.

Fees already collected and refunds: no German fee SLATE charges is paid ahead (each month's accrues at its end and posts at the quarter's closing), so the months collected at an earlier closing were each served whole and stay, and nothing is refunded. Berliner Sparkasse's Sparkassen-Card (€12.00 a year, paid ahead, refunded pro rata under its footnote 45) is a fee SLATE doesn't model.

ING (“im Folgemonat”) and Commerzbank (“monatlich”, in its distance-selling information, against its price list's “mit dem nächstfolgenden Kontoabschluss”) take the month's fee monthly where SLATE posts every German bank's at the quarter's closing: the timing differs, the sums and what a close charges don't. Not changed.

Each of the eight commands works and is tested on labelled lives abroad (each row's tests), and each row's unfinished work is none (bank.cancel_new's last item, Germany's fee to the day, is implemented above). What a played life lacks is a way to reach them: a life living outside America, which the owner's scope reset of 2026-10-09 removed and the briefs forbid restoring, or a New Haven bank offering what no US bank offers (a switching service, an arranged overdraft at the five, a money transfer card, a cooling-off period, France's overrun loan). Recommended: (b), since no work remains and (a) asks for a life the scope forbids; either way they are not counted complete.
